# Answer
## Cardiac Abnormality Events
- Over the past three weeks, cardiac abnormalities were detected on only 4 out of 21 days, indicating sporadic occurrence.
- The sole atrial fibrillation event occurred on March 10, accompanied by a premature heartbeat; all subsequent events were isolated premature heartbeats.
- Premature heartbeats occurred on March 10, 18, 20, and 27, with gaps of up to 7 days without any abnormality; no clear trend in frequency is observed.
- The data suggest no escalation in frequency or severity of cardiac events over this three-week period.

## Daily Calories Burned Through Exercise
- The weekly total calories burned show an increasing trend: 1050 kcal (week 1), 1170 kcal (week 2), and 1590 kcal (week 3).
- The peak daily calories burned increased over the weeks: 460 kcal (week 1), 450 kcal (week 2), and 580 kcal (week 3), indicating higher intensity sessions.
- While the number of active days per week remained similar (3-4 days), the average calories per active day rose, contributing to the overall upward trend.
- Despite day-to-day fluctuations due to rest days, the data indicates a clear overall increase in calories burned over the three-week period.

## Daily Sleep Duration
- The 3-week average sleep duration is approximately 342 minutes (5.7 hours), consistently below the recommended 7-9 hours, indicating chronic sleep deprivation.
- Sleep duration varies widely from 270 to 530 minutes, reflecting irregular patterns and occasional catch-up sleep.
- Weekly averages show 351 minutes (Week 1), 316 minutes (Week 2), and 359 minutes (Week 3), with a notable dip in Week 2 but no sustained trend over the period.
- Weekends often feature extended sleep, peaking on March 28 (530 min) and March 15 (470 min), suggesting accumulated weekday sleep debt, though not every weekend (e.g., March 22 had only 270 min).
- The lowest values (270 min) on March 17 and March 22 represent severe sleep restriction, highlighting risk for excessive daytime sleepiness and health impacts.
